A memorable and delicious experience
Aug 2026 • Solo
I had a fantastic meal at Gia! This restaurant is genuinely special and is 'firing on all cylinders'. Every dimension that is important to me (hospitality, design, ambiance, plating, concept/story, and of course the food itself) was a 10/10. Each dish was not just delicious but told a story about the feeling of home, spotlighted local ingredients, and was presented beautifully. I loved the flipcard notes to read more about the dish. The sauces were really something special, I had some sauces that I can't get out of my head days later... The meal itself was the perfect amount of food (I did not leave hungry) and the staff did a great job explaining the dishes and answering any questions. The design of the restaurant is so beautiful, the walls are such a lovely shade of green. I dined here alone and the team made me feel so special and welcome, as you can see from the picture I was given a really special table. Sometimes fine dining can feel overly formal / intimidating but here I really felt the sense of home and comfort. I absolutely will dine here again. Thank you to everyone who made my experience so memorable!!

Disappointing
Jun 2026 • Friends
Out of the eight-course menu, only the starter and the final dessert stood out. The rest of the dishes were extremely basic, lacked flavour, and were far from what I would expect from a Michelin-starred restaurant. Honestly, I've had much better meals at small local restaurants in Hanoi for a fraction of the price.

The service was equally disappointing. Although the restaurant was almost empty, we were seated right by the entrance. At the end of the meal, they initially refused to deduct my deposit from the bill, insisting it would be refunded in two weeks. Only after speaking with the manager did they agree to deduct it from the final payment. To top it off, there were two of us dining, yet they gave us only one takeaway gift bag, and I had to ask for a second one.

The venue itself is beautiful, but that's about the only positive. I genuinely don't understand why this restaurant has a Michelin star. There are countless places in Hanoi where you'll enjoy far better quality food for much less. I wouldn't return.

Modern Vietnamese Flavors Come Alive in a Playful, Interactive Tasting Experience at Gia, Hanoi, Vietnam
Nov 2025 • Friends
Gia Restaurant in Hanoi was an experience—where regional Vietnamese ingredients are reimagined into modern, artful bites that feel both familiar and completely fresh. A few parts of dinner were interactive which added a playful twist that made the evening more genuinely fun and immersive. I loved how the team showcased ingredients in their original form along with transforming plated dish—it’s a small detail that makes a big impact. And the mocktail pairing? Perfectly curated and every bit as thoughtful as a wine flight. A very good dining experience from start to finish.

Food Needed a Louder Voice
Jul 2025 • Solo
My much-anticipated visit to Gia finally happened. Service was impeccable. Plates were small works of art. Yet the presentation often outshone the taste, as many dishes felt bland and underseasoned. This was most evident in the modern take on beef soup. Its broth’s subtle bitterness was a creative risk, but it sacrificed the deep, savory warmth that I craved. The saving grace was the beverage program: both the caffeine-free strawberry coffee and the tamarind coconut were inventive and exceptional. Given the seasonally changing menu and such memorable drinks, I’d consider visiting again.

Glad we tried it, but won’t be going back
Apr 2025 • Couples
The restaurant is nicely decorated, with a lot of space between tables. The tasting menu has enough dishes to fill you up. The food is presented very nicely. Those are the pros. Now for the cons - some of the dishes are bland. There’s a lot of herbs and spices and sauces in Vietnamese cuisine so I wonder why even though the dishes look like it has a lot of components, there just wasn’t enough taste. 

I asked the waitress for the wine menu and my partner and I were discussing between ourselves how the prices are vastly different to Spain where we last went. Nothing bad, we were even laughing about it, that we were drinking from lunch time over there. The sommelier overheard and came to our table and told us that the wine tax is a lot, therefore the prices will definitely be higher. I said sure, we also have wine tax in our country. She looked so displeased and there was some attitude when I finally ordered a bottle. 

They took us to the kitchen to say hello and see the chefs at work, which is a nice touch. They moved our drinks and belongings while we were upstairs. Dessert was served in the front of the restaurant even though the dinner area wasn’t full. 

Glad we went for the experience, but manage your expectations
